thread:
maria: kicking off ap-northeast-2 hybrid cluster bring-up. control plane is kubeadm on edge-ctrl-01, workers will be in EKS (apne2) using GPU nodegroups (A10G). preflight mostly green, need someone to validate CNI, IAM & node->control-plane network rules. runbook: https://runbooks.internal/redwood/apne2-hybrid-bootstrap

aj: on it. i can validate SGs/route tables and eksctl nodegroup config. remind me which AMI + GPU driver we pin?
	maria: we want the vendor AMI with CUDA 12 + NVIDIA 535 drivers, kernel tested on 6.1. pinned AMI in infra repo: infra/images/apne2/gpu-ami-v3.
	raj: quota FYI — apne2 has low p4 quotas. talked to cloud-ops; they can open to 8 vGPUs if we provide a build/design doc. for now we should start with 2x A10G nodegroup and validate autoscaling.
	kai: quick note about CNI — calico manifests in infra/k8s/addons/calico/apne2.yaml have IPPool set to 10.32.0.0/12 which clashes with on-prem edge LAN. we should change to 10.48.0.0/12 before applying.
	maria: good catch. I'll update the runbook. also need to ensure kube-apiserver has --requestheader-client-ca-file for our edge mTLS. kubeadm config snippet for control plane: ```apiVersion: kubeadm.k8s.io/v1beta3kind: ClusterConfigurationapiServer:  extraArgs:  - "requestheader-client-ca-file=/etc/kubernetes/pki/front-proxy-ca.crt"networking: podSubnet: "10.48.0.0/12"```

aj: for EKS nodegroup we use an eksctl config like: ```apiVersion: eksctl.io/v1alpha5kind: ClusterMetadata:  name: rw-apne2-hybridnodeGroups: - name: gpu-a10g  instanceType: a10g.xlarge  desiredCapacity: 2  minSize: 1  maxSize: 4  ssh: allow: true  labels: {role: gpu}  iam: withAddonPolicies: {imageBuilder: true}``` make sure iamRole has AmazonEKSWorkerNodePolicy + EC2ContainerRegistryReadOnly + SSM.

maria: deploying nodegroup now. tagging nodes with clusterID so cloud routing rules pick them up. will post progress.

infra-bot: provisioning job started for nodegroup gpu-a10g (job id: prov-20260301-009). status: LAUNCHING

ryan: when nodes join, run this quick validation: ```kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep gpu``` then validate device plugin and drivers: ```kubectl get daemonset nvidia-device-plugin -n kube-system && kubectl logs -l name=nvidia-device-plugin -n kube-system``` finally: `kubectl exec -it <gpu-pod> -- nvidia-smi`

kai: also validate metrics and kubelet flags: `--feature-gates=DevicePlugins=true` and kubelet config has allowed unsafe sysctls if needed. check kube-proxy mode (ipvs vs iptables) — we use ipvs for perf.

maria: nodegroup is now in Ready state, 2 nodes joined (names: ip-10-48-0-12, ip-10-48-0-13). starting GPU driver DaemonSet apply.

infra-bot: prov-20260301-009 status: RUNNING. nodes registered: 2. attaching logs to thread: https://internal-logs/streams/prov-20260301-009

aj: verified SGs. opened port 10250 from control plane CIDR and allowed node-to-node pod CIDR. route table has route to on-prem via transit-gw. :thumbsup:

ryan: GPU plugin and drivers are healthy. `nvidia-smi` shows 1 GPU per node. running small perf job: `kubectl run --rm -it --image=nvcr.io/nvidia/cuda:12.1-base ntest -- nvidia-smi` returned expected output.

kai: CNI fixed, I patched calico IPPool to 10.48.0.0/12 and restarted calico pods. pods scheduling across nodes looks good. flannel sidecar not installed, confirmed.

maria: thanks team. next: handoff to ops for final validation and cost gating. ops-oncall — can you run the cost / quota checklist and sign off? linking checklist: https://runbooks.internal/redwood/cost-checklist

ops-oncall: taking handoff. i'll verify quotas, autoscaler policies, and create a short cost projection for expected 99th percentile traffic. ETA 2 hours. will test failover to fallback region as well.

maria: perfect. leaving notes in runbook about network gotcha and pinned AMI. if ops signs off, i'll tag this as ready-for-prod and schedule rollout window. :white_check_mark:
